value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Saint Paul's residential solar customers this session; Xcel Energy is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Saint Paul Department of Safety and Inspections (DSI)
permit_authority.notes: Minnesota's State Building Code is mandatory in the seven-county Twin Cities metro area (which includes Saint Paul/Ramsey County) and is notably not locally amendable — the same uniform statewide code applying to Minneapolis, researched separately this session (see mn-hennepin-minneapolis-xcel). DSI is Saint Paul's own consolidated permitting authority, processing building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and elevator permits (over 32,000/year).

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical statewide Minnesota net-metering framework notes on the Minneapolis record (mn-hennepin-minneapolis-xcel) — codified in Minn. Stat. 216B.164, with residential systems under 40kW AC receiving 1:1 retail-rate compensation.

value.name: Completed Electrical Permit Application, submitted with the applicable fee through the City's PAULIE online platform

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Solar PV Systems Electrical Permit page, which addresses the electrical permit specifically (fees, inspection process). A separate building permit covering roof/mounting structural review may also apply — the page fetched this session focused on the electrical permit process only, not a full combined checklist.

value: The contractor must be present for all Solar/PV electrical permit inspections
Residential (one- and two-family) contractors can schedule inspections online
Inspection requests are handled by calling the inspector between 7:30 a.m. and 9:00 a.m., Monday through Friday
All work must comply with the latest National Electrical Code as adopted by Minnesota

timeline_days.notes: The City's own page does not state a specific review-to-issuance day count; it does state the permit expires if work does not commence within 180 days of issuance, and exterior work on a single- or two-family dwelling must be completed within one year.

other_conditions: Permits expire if work does not commence within 180 days of issuance
Exterior work on a single- or two-family dwelling (including garages) must be completed within one year

The 40kW AC figure recorded here reflects the statewide net-metering threshold for the standard 1:1 retail-rate compensation tier (per Minn. Stat. 216B.164), not a separate City permit-eligibility limit

permit_fees.notes: Fees are calculated based on the system's total estimated AC energy output in kW, with fractional kilowatts rounded to the nearest whole number. This is the electrical permit fee only; a separate building permit fee may apply if structural/roof work is also required.

rebates.notes: No specific Saint Paul or statewide Minnesota rebate dollar amount was independently confirmed from a primary source this session — left null rather than guessed.
